scenarios.name: prefix_is_not_a_ballot
scenarios.what: A runtime-opened foil vote; `!vote the-d` is a unique prefix the runtime refuses.

op.question: Which foil shall the Host summon?

scenarios.name: summon_in_crowd_poll_is_not_a_ballot
scenarios.what: An op-opened crowd poll over the foils; `!summon` lands only in a foil vote.

scenarios.name: crowd_poll_ranks_case_index_revote
scenarios.what: Rank weights, min rank, case-insensitive text, a 1-based index and a re-vote.

scenarios.name: summon_and_vote_in_foil_vote
scenarios.what: In a foil vote both `!summon` and `!vote` count; a second summon moves the ballot.

op.question: Which foil shall the Host summon?

scenarios.name: summon_batch_opens_foil_vote
scenarios.what: One batch opens a foil vote: lines before its first known-foil `!summon` find no poll; that line and every ballot after it count.

op.question: Which foil shall the Host summon?

scenarios.name: trimmed_exact_text
scenarios.what: Surrounding whitespace in the option is trimmed; inner text must match exactly.

scenarios.name: unknown_option_and_out_of_range_index
scenarios.what: Unknown text, index 0 and an index past the end are not ballots.

scenarios.name: index_before_text
scenarios.what: A number is an index first; only an out-of-range number falls back to exact text.

scenarios.name: ascii_only_case_folding
scenarios.what: Case folds for ASCII letters only: `ü` does not match `Ü`.

scenarios.name: under_rank_revote_keeps_the_ballot
scenarios.what: A viewer below the min rank is refused; a re-vote naming no option keeps the earlier ballot.

scenarios.name: zero_voter_row
scenarios.what: An option nobody chose stays in the tally with 0 voters and 0 weight.

scenarios.name: command_from_text
scenarios.what: A chat line with no parsed `command`: the runtime parses its text, the screen does not.

scenarios.name: crowd_poll_named_like_a_foil_vote
scenarios.what: A crowd poll the brain named `foil-vote-7`: the screen reads the id as a foil vote.

deviations.note: The screen counts only a chat line's parsed `command`; the runtime also parses a line's text when the adapter left `command` empty.
The stream does not carry a poll's kind: the screen recognises a foil vote by the runtime-minted `foil-vote-` id, so a crowd poll the brain named that way takes `!summon` on screen only.
